messages.author: e76bf5e76da333a2
messages.subject: Uniform Prior on standard devation
parts:
Dears
 
I come for your usually support.  I learn the question is asked many times by users.
Here is what I want;

I have a random effect b_i,

        b_i ~N(0,precision=tau.b)

I want to assume the following prior

tau.b <- pow(sigma.b,-2)
         sigma.b~dunif(0,100)

I saw the flat, logflat and logiflat prior on http://www.r-inla.org/models/priors, but the three priors listed doesn't correspond to the above prior. Is there any want who trays to implement using "expression"?

Kind regards
Belay

messages.author: b453c29749de564d
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Uniform Prior on standard devation
parts:
use this one instead

inla.doc("pc.prec")


its a much more sensible choice. setting lambda to small gives you the
uniform, but I wouldn't do that.

H

messages.author: 9940b4fcc153c7d7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Uniform Prior on standard devation
parts:
About the question, you could implement such a prior using expression. But you would have to transform it to the INLA-parameter (log tau).

The prior you suggest, as Håvard says, is a bad prior (the pc.prec is better in all ways). But if you are doing this for comparison reasons... you can do it.

Haakon

messages.author: 9940b4fcc153c7d7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Uniform Prior on standard devation
parts:
In that case:

You cannot cut off the prior at 100. However, you can put the log probability to -1000. If the posterior is in the vicinity of the cutoff point, the inla-function will be "confused".
